I’ll read the continuation note and repository guidance, then carry out the recommended next steps.

The note makes the row-selector test the first gate: a smooth complete family adds principal rows that the exceptional set excludes. I’m checking their exact contribution before using that enlargement. In parallel, I’ve assigned separate checks of the sixth-power budget and the plain-divisor transform.

The sixth-power calculation identifies a gap in the enlargement route. When the plain and prime profiles retain principal main terms, the available inverse bound exceeds the target budget by at least \(19/375-\rho\) in the exponent near prime capacity. That is a shortfall in the available estimate, not a disproof of the target. I’m also checking when the actual profiles make those main terms vanish.

There is a proved partial result: when the actual plain profile has zero integral, the added sixth-power rows fit comfortably below the target. The divisor analysis also found an exact way to absorb the live plain divisor into an averaged label, but the Cauchy cost and conductor widths still prevent the existing theorem from applying. I’m recording both results and their limits.

The updated manuscript compiles successfully. The separate agent checks agree on the selector budget and mean-zero subcase. I’m finishing the links and review records; the notes make clear that both the complete-family route and the divisor-first transfer still need estimates beyond those currently available.

Continued the investigation and updated the [manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-character-amplification/manuscript.tex).

- **Selector gate:** existing bounds do not justify complete-family enlargement. Proved a partial result controlling principal rows when the plain profile has zero integral.
- **Divisor analysis:** derived the exact transformed coefficient and Cauchy cost; the existing theorem’s width conditions still fail.

Saved detailed notes, reproducible arithmetic, and scoped reviews. Exact checks pass, and the updated manuscript compiles successfully.

The required **1/5000 mixed saving remains unproved**. The current conditional candidate remains **7/8 − 1/24000**; the next research step requires a new estimate preserving the exceptional-row selector.
